Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

"}, "control": {}}

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

answer:
Try cutting soft things and combining them twice. Don't combine things more than twice. For example: Paper and flower cut both, combine both after they are cut and frame it. Should land 100 points. Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

"}, "control": {}}

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

"}, "control": {}}

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

Grab the beans but don't soak them, just cook them

Soak rice in water and then cook on stove

Then, combine the cooked beans with the soaked rice

Cook the bacon with stove. Then, put bread on TOP of bacon

Cook fish on stove. Then, add fresh mushrooms but don't cook them. Then, add corn on top of fish and mushroom

Cook egg on stove. Then cook potato separately with stove. Then, place potato on top of egg.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

Welcome! In this experiment, you will play a game where you use tools and combine ingredients to make new items.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

"}, "control": {}}

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

"}, "control": {}}

Soak rice in water and then cook on stove

Cook the bacon with stove. Then, put bread on TOP of bacon

Cook fish on stove. Then, add fresh mushrooms but don't cook them. Then, add corn on top of fish and mushroom

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

answer:
Try to put things that make sense together.
Here are two trios that will gives you points for at least
two of the rounds (don't add anything else):
Frame + Scissors + Newspaper = 45 points
Scissors + Cardboard + Pinecone = 55 points

I didn't realize the notes were usable for the message at the end for the next person.  So another piece of advice is right down the best combos, duos and trios each round (if you find any 20 point or better) and put them on the scratch pad for your later use but also for the next person.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

Here are tips for several different rounds to maximize your points:

Grab the beans but don't soak them, just cook them

Soak rice in water and then cook on stove

Then, combine the cooked beans with the soaked rice

Cook the bacon with stove. Then, put bread on TOP of bacon

Cook fish on stove. Then, add fresh mushrooms but don't cook them. Then, add corn on top of fish and mushroom

Cook egg on stove. Then cook potato separately with stove. Then, place potato on top of egg.

Cook beans, potatoes and mushrooms separately with stove. Then, place potatoes on top of beans. Then, place mushrooms on top of potatoes.

You can combine ingredients to make stews.

most liquids can be filtered, and solids can be extracted with vial. Do that first.. Similar themes go well together. (unicorn +rose or basilisk + batwing)

I got like 0 points on all of them bc I was overcomplicating them, you really only need 2 ingredients to get to 100. I found that these three recipes give a lot of points:

Filtered kraken ink and tree sap blend is 100 points, first filter tree sap, then filter kraken ink, then combine.

Filter honey nectar, then filter kraken ink, combine those two together for 100 points.

Filter kraken ink, vial unicorn extract, then combine those for 60 points

question: message
answer:
One thing I learned while playing is that the tools matter less than the ingredient combinations. The main pattern I found is that combining a positive-value mundane ingredient with a positive-value magical ingredient gives you 100 points, but only if both ingredients share the same state of matter (for example, both liquids or both solids). This rule helped me figure out the best pairings quickly.

Reliable 100-point combinations:
-Mushroom + Mandrake
-Mushroom + Dragon Scale
-Mandrake + Amber
-Mandrake + Obsidian
-Unicorn + Bat Wing
-Dandelion + Dragon Scale
-Rose + Dragon Scale
-Amber + Dragon Scale
-Mandrake + Bat Wing

Solid 60-point combinations:
-Dragon + Mandrake
-Obsidian + Frog
-Amber + Dandelion
-Rose + Amber
-Mushroom + Rose

Things to avoid:
-Combining two magical ingredients (usually gave me very negative values)
-Mixing ingredients with different states of matter when trying for a high-value combo.

question: post_experiment_survey
answer: {"strategy": "In the first animal game I wasn't paying attention at first to the fact that the ingredients were all divided into set categories that could be viewed, so I was examining each animal individually and recording what 1, 2, or 3 changes of each type would do. For each change (growth or mutation) it became obvious that there was a maximum and a minimum before causing detrimental effects. But it became easier once I realized that the categories in every game were absolute (always large/medium/small, land/air/sea, artificial/natural, soft/hard), rather than being based on individual items. At that point I only needed to record the effects of changes on each category of item, which made it faster.", "message": "I figured out the key in each game and just explained how to win; there is no reason to give people riddles to figure out. I really dislike when teachers do that, make you waste time figuring out some secret instead of telling you how it's done so you can quickly reverse engineer the logic behind it and continue progressing. Logic games have a place in education, but imagine if previous generations didn't leave manuals or textbooks explaining things, they only left us \"hints\" to discover what they had already discovered... scientific progress would be dramatically slower.", "enjoyable": "It was interesting, in retrospect it reminded me of taxonomy and how science tries to classify everything by a particular kind. I used to make similar databases for materials when I was young (classifying woods or rocks or fabrics by strength, hardness, etc.). Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

You will play the game for several rounds. In each round, you will have the same tools, but different starting ingredients. As you play the game, you will learn the rules that determine how items combine and how valuable each item is. These rules might be intuitive, but they might also be unintuitive, so you should try different combinations and see what happens.

Each item has a value shown next to its name. Your score in each round will be the value of the most valuable item you created. For example, if you had the two items below in your inventory, your score would be 16.

Your score can't go below 0, even if all of your items have negative values. The maximum possible score is 100 in every round. You will earn a bonus of up to $1 based on your performance.

Ingredients all have features that determine how they combine with other ingredients and how valuable they are. These features change when you apply tools or combine them with other ingredients. You can see an ingredient's features by hovering over it with your mouse.

You can take notes throughout the experiment using the scratchpad on the right side of the screen. The text in the scratchpad will stay from round to round.

It is possible that one of your items might get stuck somewhere where you can't click it. If this happens, you can refresh the page and your inventory will be preserved.

When you are ready, click the "Start" button to play a practice game.

"}, "control": {}}
